references.text: Isaiah uses the same image of head and tail to describe leaders and false prophets in Israel, as a contrast to the blessing of being the head and not the tail.
The opposite situation is described as a curse: foreigners will be the head and Israel the tail if they do not obey the Lord's commands.
The same promise to be exalted above all nations is repeated as part of the covenant blessings for obedience to the Lord's commands.
The promise to rule over other nations and not be ruled oneself, linked to obedience to God's commands.
The fundamental principle of blessing for obedience to the Lord's commands, which underlies the promise in 28:13.
Paul urges believers not to be conformed to this world but to be transformed—an echo of the call to be above, not below.
Proverbs confirms that the borrower is a slave to the lender—the same principle of being above or below.
